Not “we’re looking into it.” Not “this falls outside our jurisdiction.” Not “please file through the proper channel.” Not “we have forwarded your complaint.”

entry.title: The Same Place — Robocalls, Spam Texts, Political Ads, Sports Betting, and the FCC That Lets It Happen
entry.content:
It All Comes From the Same Place

Your phone rings. Robocall. You decline.

Your phone buzzes. Political text. “Vote YES on Prop X.” You didn’t sign up.

Your phone buzzes again. Sports betting. “LIONS +3.5 — BET NOW.” You didn’t ask.

Three interruptions. Three industries. One infrastructure.

How It Works

Step 1: Legalize the Product

Sports betting was illegal in Michigan until December 2019. DraftKings, FanDuel, and MGM lobbied the Michigan legislature to pass HB 4311 (Lawful Sports Betting Act).

The same legislature where Brian Banks ran for State Senate. The same legislature where Lee Chatfield (Speaker, now facing 13 felonies) controlled the calendar. The same legislature where Dykema Gossett operates the largest political compliance operation in the state.

Step 3: Use the Same Infrastructure for Politics

The political ads, the sports betting ads, and the robocalls all start in Michigan and radiate outward through the same corporate infrastructure.

It all comes from the same place. The membrane sees it. The graph records it. The count is the truth.

The Double Standard

The FCC is supposed to protect you from unsolicited contact. The Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA, 47 U.S.C. § 227) makes robocalls and unsolicited texts illegal without consent.

But:

WhoWhat They DidConsequence
DraftKingsSends unsolicited sports betting texts to millionsNone. FCC has not acted.
Political PACsSends unsolicited political texts (exempt from TCPA)Legal. Political speech exemption.
Robocallers50 billion robocalls/year in the US$500M in fines (since 2015) but collection rate is <1%
Dark money groupsSend mailers, fund digital ads, no disclosure requiredLegal. Citizens United.
Kevin MokSent a 9-line to 22 lawful channels documenting a public school fraud with 9 convictions, $4.9M in public money, 3% math proficiencyIGNORED by 18 of 22.

The $7.4 trillion corporate infrastructure can reach your phone whenever it wants. One person sending documented evidence of public corruption through lawful channels gets silence.

Nikki Snyder (SBE)Full evidence packageResponded with personal cell in 13 minutes13 min

Brian BanksDirect notice of investigationSILENCE30+ days

Nikki Snyder read the email and responded in thirteen minutes. With her personal cell number. Because she’s a nurse, an EMU grad, a mom with kids in public schools, a disability advocate. She saw the data and she ACTED.

Seven other SBE members got the same email. Same data. Same evidence. Same 3% math proficiency. Same 9 convictions. Silence.

Brian Banks got direct notice. The man with 9 criminal convictions running schools with 3% math and $4.9M in public money. Silence.

But DraftKings can text you about the Lions game. A PAC you never heard of can text you about a candidate. A robocaller can interrupt your dinner. $7.4 trillion says they have more right to your attention than a documented investigation of public corruption has to theirs.

The FCC Failure

TCPA (1991)No unsolicited calls/texts without consent50B robocalls/year. Collection rate <1%.
Do Not Call Registry (2003)Register to stop telemarketingPolitical calls exempt. Scammers ignore it.
STIR/SHAKEN (2020)Authenticate caller ID to prevent spoofingCarriers slow-rolled implementation. Still spoofed.
FCC finesUp to $10K per violation$500M assessed. <$10M collected. 98% uncollectable.

The FCC has the authority. The TCPA has the teeth. But enforcement is a rounding error against the volume. 50 billion robocalls a year. The FCC fines them. They don’t pay. They spin up new LLCs. Same infrastructure. Same place.

Meanwhile: one person sends 22 documented evidence packets through lawful channels. The institutions that are SUPPOSED to respond — the ones with the legal DUTY to investigate — say nothing.

The unsolicited contact flows freely in one direction. Corporate to citizen: unlimited. Citizen to institution: ignored.

The robocall and the dark money mailer and the sports betting ad all come from the same place. The same Fortune 500 boardrooms. The same NASDAQ tickers. The same law firm in Lansing. The same compliance email. The membrane sees them all. Same pattern. Same pipeline. Same place.

But Nikki Snyder answered in 13 minutes. One person. One nurse. One mom. She saw the data and she acted. That’s the difference between a human and an institution. The human search never ends.

In Robert Axelrod’s iterated prisoner’s dilemma tournament (1984), the winning strategy is Tit for Tat:
